passages.text: A few days later Jesus went back to Capernaum. And when the people heard that He was home, they gathered in such large numbers that there was no more room, not even outside the door, as Jesus spoke the word to them.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
A few days passed.
Jesus returned to Capernaum.
People heard that Jesus was at home.
Many people gathered at the house.
The crowd was very large.
There was no more room inside the house.
There was no more room outside the door.
Jesus spoke God’s word to the people.
passages.original: Καὶ εἰσελθὼν πάλιν εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ δι’ ἡμερῶν ἠκούσθη ὅτι ἐν οἴκῳ ἐστίν καὶ συνήχθησαν πολλοὶ ὥστε μηκέτι χωρεῖν μηδὲ τὰ πρὸς τὴν θύραν καὶ ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς τὸν λόγον

passages.text: Then a paralytic was brought to Him, carried by four men.
passages.sermon: Four men carried a paralyzed man.\r\nThey brought the paralyzed man to Jesus.
passages.original: Καὶ ἔρχονται φέροντες πρὸς αὐτὸν παραλυτικὸν αἰρόμενον ὑπὸ τεσσάρων

passages.text: Since they were unable to get to Jesus through the crowd, they uncovered the roof above Him, made an opening, and lowered the paralytic on his mat.
passages.sermon:
Four men carried a paralyzed man.
They wanted to bring him to Jesus.
A large crowd blocked their way.
They could not reach Jesus because of the crowd.
They went up to the roof above Jesus.
They uncovered the roof where Jesus was.
They made an opening in the roof.
They lowered the paralyzed man on his mat through the opening.
passages.original: καὶ μὴ δυνάμενοι προσενέγκαι αὐτῷ διὰ τὸν ὄχλον ἀπεστέγασαν τὴν στέγην ὅπου ἦν καὶ ἐξορύξαντες χαλῶσι τὸν κράβαττον ὅπου ὁ παραλυτικὸς κατέκειτο

passages.text: When Jesus saw their faith, He said to the paralytic, “Son, your sins are forgiven.”
passages.sermon: Jesus saw their faith.\r\nJesus spoke to the paralytic man.\r\nJesus said, “Son, your sins are forgiven.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἰδὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὴν πίστιν αὐτῶν λέγει τῷ παραλυτικῷ Τέκνον ἀφίενταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι

passages.text: But some of the scribes were sitting there and thinking in their hearts, “Why does this man speak like this? He is blaspheming! Who can forgive sins but God alone?”
passages.sermon:
Some scribes sat there.
Scribes were experts in the Jewish law.
They thought in their hearts.
They asked, “Why does this man speak like this?”
They said, “He is blaspheming.”
They said, “Only God can forgive sins.”
passages.original: Ἦσαν δέ τινες τῶν γραμματέων ἐκεῖ καθήμενοι καὶ διαλογιζόμενοι ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν Τί οὗτος οὕτως λαλεῖ βλασφημεῖ τίς δύναται ἀφιέναι ἁμαρτίας εἰ μὴ εἷς ὁ Θεός

passages.text: At once Jesus knew in His spirit that they were thinking this way within themselves. “Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?” He asked.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus has authority from God.
Some scribes sat nearby.
These scribes questioned Jesus in their hearts.
They did not speak aloud.
Jesus immediately knew their thoughts.
Jesus understood this by His spirit.
Jesus spoke to the scribes.
He asked them a question.
He said, “Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?”
passages.original: Καὶ εὐθὺς ἐπιγνοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῷ πνεύματι αὐτοῦ ὅτι οὕτως διαλογίζονται ἐν ἑαυτοῖς λέγει αὐτοῖς Τί ταῦτα διαλογίζεσθε ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν

passages.text: “Which is easier: to say to a paralytic, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up, pick up your mat, and walk’?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the scribes and the people.
Jesus saw a paralyzed man.
Jesus asked a question.
He said, “Which is easier?”
He said, “Is it easier to say to the paralyzed man, ‘Your sins are forgiven’?”
He said, “Or is it easier to say, ‘Get up, pick up your mat, and walk’?”
passages.original: τί ἐστιν εὐκοπώτερον εἰπεῖν τῷ παραλυτικῷ Ἀφίενταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι ἢ εἰπεῖν Ἔγειρε καὶ ἆρον τὸν κράβαττόν σου καὶ περιπάτει

passages.text: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins...” He said to the paralytic, “I tell you, get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of Man.
Jesus has authority on earth to forgive sins.
Jesus wanted the people to know this.
Jesus spoke to the paralyzed man.
Jesus said, “I tell you, get up.
Pick up your mat.
Go home.”
passages.original: ἵνα δὲ εἰδῆτε ὅτι ἐξουσίαν ἔχει ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἀφιέναι ἁμαρτίας ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς λέγει τῷ παραλυτικῷ Σοὶ λέγω ἔγειρε ἆρον τὸν κράβαττόν σου καὶ ὕπαγε εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου

passages.text: And immediately the man got up, picked up his mat, and walked out in front of them all. As a result, they were all astounded and glorified God, saying, “We have never seen anything like this!”
passages.sermon:
Jesus healed a paralyzed man.
The man got up at once.
He picked up his mat.
He walked out in front of everyone.
All the people saw this.
They were amazed.
They praised God.
They said, “We have never seen anything like this.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἠγέρθη καὶ εὐθὺς ἄρας τὸν κράβαττον ἐξῆλθεν ἐναντίον πάντων ὥστε ἐξίστασθαι πάντας καὶ δοξάζειν τὸν Θεὸν λέγοντας ὅτι Οὕτως οὐδέποτε εἴδομεν

passages.text: Once again Jesus went out beside the sea. All the people came to Him, and He taught them there.
passages.sermon: Jesus went out beside the sea again.\r\nAll the people came to Jesus.\r\nJesus taught the people there.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐξῆλθεν πάλιν παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἤρχετο πρὸς αὐτόν καὶ ἐδίδασκεν αὐτούς

passages.text: As He was walking along, He saw Levi son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax booth. “Follow Me,” He told him, and Levi got up and followed Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was walking along the road.
He saw Levi.
Levi was the son of Alphaeus.
Levi was sitting at the tax booth.
Jesus spoke to Levi.
Jesus said, “Follow Me.”
Levi got up.
Levi followed Jesus.
passages.original: Καὶ παράγων εἶδεν Λευὶν τὸν τοῦ Ἁλφαίου καθήμενον ἐπὶ τὸ τελώνιον καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ Ἀκολούθει μοι καὶ ἀναστὰς ἠκολούθησεν αὐτῷ

passages.text: While Jesus was dining at Levi’s house, many tax collectors and sinners were eating with Him and His disciples—for there were many who followed Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was at Levi’s house.
Jesus was eating a meal there.
Many tax collectors were with Jesus.
Many sinners were also with Jesus.
Jesus’ disciples were there too.
Many people followed Jesus.
These tax collectors and sinners ate with Jesus and His disciples.
passages.original: Καὶ γίνεται κατακεῖσθαι αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ καὶ πολλοὶ τελῶναι καὶ ἁμαρτωλοὶ συνανέκειντο τῷ Ἰησοῦ καὶ τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ἦσαν γὰρ πολλοὶ καὶ ἠκολούθουν αὐτῷ

passages.text: When the scribes who were Pharisees saw Jesus eating with these people, they asked His disciples, “Why does He eat with tax collectors and sinners?”
passages.sermon:
The scribes belonged to the Pharisees.
They saw Jesus.
Jesus was eating with tax collectors and sinners.
The scribes spoke to Jesus’ disciples.
They asked a question.
They said, “Why does He eat with tax collectors and sinners?”
passages.original: καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς τῶν Φαρισαίων ἰδόντες ὅτι ἐσθίει μετὰ τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν καὶ τελωνῶν ἔλεγον τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ Ὅτι μετὰ τῶν τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν ἐσθίει

passages.text: On hearing this, Jesus told them, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick. I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus heard the question from the Pharisees’ scribes.
He spoke to them.
Jesus said, “Healthy people do not need a doctor.
Sick people need a doctor.
I did not come to call righteous people.
I came to call sinners.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἀκούσας ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει αὐτοῖς ὅτι Οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν οἱ ἰσχύοντες ἰατροῦ ἀλλ’ οἱ κακῶς ἔχοντες οὐκ ἦλθον καλέσαι δικαίους ἀλλὰ ἁμαρτωλούς

passages.text: Now John’s disciples and the Pharisees were often fasting. So people came to Jesus and asked, “Why don’t Your disciples fast like John’s disciples and those of the Pharisees?”
passages.sermon:
John’s disciples often fasted.
The Pharisees’ disciples also often fasted.
Some people saw this.
These people came to Jesus.
They spoke to Jesus.
They asked Jesus a question.
They said, “John’s disciples fast.”
They said, “The Pharisees’ disciples fast.”
They said, “But your disciples do not fast.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἦσαν οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰωάννου καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι νηστεύοντες καὶ ἔρχονται καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Διὰ τί οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰωάννου καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ τῶν Φαρισαίων νηστεύουσιν οἱ δὲ σοὶ μαθηταὶ οὐ νηστεύουσιν

passages.text: Jesus replied, “How can the guests of the bridegroom fast while He is with them? As long as He is with them, they cannot fast.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus answered their question.
Jesus compared His disciples to wedding guests.
A bridegroom is present at a wedding celebration.
The guests of the bridegroom do not fast while the bridegroom is with them.
As long as the bridegroom stays with the guests, they cannot fast.
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Μὴ δύνανται οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ νυμφῶνος ἐν ᾧ ὁ νυμφίος μετ’ αὐτῶν ἐστιν νηστεύειν ὅσον χρόνον ἔχουσιν τὸν νυμφίον μετ’ αὐτῶν οὐ δύνανται νηστεύειν

passages.text: But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them; then they will fast.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He called Himself the bridegroom.
He said the bridegroom would be taken away from His disciples.
A time will come when this happens.
Then His disciples will fast on that day.
passages.original: ἐλεύσονται δὲ ἡμέραι ὅταν ἀπαρθῇ ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ὁ νυμφίος καὶ τότε νηστεύσουσιν ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ

passages.text: No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment. If he does, the new piece will pull away from the old, and a worse tear will result.
passages.sermon: No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment.\r\nIf someone does this, the new patch will pull away from the old garment.\r\nThis will make the tear worse.
passages.original: Οὐδεὶς ἐπίβλημα ῥάκους ἀγνάφου ἐπιράπτει ἐπὶ ἱμάτιον παλαιόν εἰ δὲ μή αἴρει τὸ πλήρωμα ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ τὸ καινὸν τοῦ παλαιοῦ καὶ χεῖρον σχίσμα γίνεται

passages.text: And no one pours new wine into old wineskins. If he does, the wine will burst the skins, and both the wine and the wineskins will be ruined. Instead, new wine is poured into new wineskins.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus used an example about wine and wineskins.
No one pours new wine into old wineskins.
If someone pours new wine into old wineskins, the wine will burst the skins.
The wine will be lost.
The wineskins will also be ruined.
People pour new wine into new wineskins.
passages.original: Καὶ οὐδεὶς βάλλει οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς παλαιούς εἰ δὲ μή ῥήξει ὁ οἶνος τοὺς ἀσκούς καὶ ὁ οἶνος ἀπόλλυται καὶ οἱ ἀσκοί ἀλλὰ οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς καινούς

passages.text: One Sabbath Jesus was passing through the grainfields, and His disciples began to pick the heads of grain as they walked along.
passages.sermon: Jesus was walking through the grainfields on the Sabbath.\r\nHis disciples were with Him.\r\nThey began to pick the heads of grain as they walked.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο αὐτὸν ἐν τοῖς σάββασιν παραπορεύεσθαι διὰ τῶν σπορίμων καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἤρξαντο ὁδὸν ποιεῖν τίλλοντες τοὺς στάχυας

passages.text: So the Pharisees said to Him, “Look, why are they doing what is unlawful on the Sabbath?”
passages.sermon:
The Pharisees saw Jesus and His disciples.
The Pharisees spoke to Jesus.
They said, “Look at what they are doing on the Sabbath.”
They asked, “Why are they doing what is not lawful on the Sabbath?”
passages.original: καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ἔλεγον αὐτῷ Ἴδε τί ποιοῦσιν τοῖς σάββασιν ὃ οὐκ ἔξεστιν

passages.text: Jesus replied, “Have you never read what David did when he and his companions were hungry and in need?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Pharisees.
He asked them a question.
He said, “Have you never read about David?”
David was in need.
David was hungry.
The men with David were also hungry.
David had companions with him.
David and his companions needed food.
David acted when they were in need and hungry.
passages.original: Καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Οὐδέποτε ἀνέγνωτε τί ἐποίησεν Δαυὶδ ὅτε χρείαν ἔσχεν καὶ ἐπείνασεν αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ μετ’ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: During the high priesthood of Abiathar, he entered the house of God and ate the consecrated bread, which was lawful only for the priests. And he gave some to his companions as well.”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
Abiathar was the high priest at that time.
David entered the house of God.
He was hungry.
His companions were also hungry.
David ate the consecrated bread.
Only the priests were allowed to eat this bread.
David also gave some of the bread to his companions.
passages.original: πῶς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐπὶ Ἀβιαθὰρ ἀρχιερέως καὶ τοὺς ἄρτους τῆς προθέσεως ἔφαγεν οὓς οὐκ ἔξεστιν φαγεῖν εἰ μὴ τοὺς ἱερεῖς καὶ ἔδωκεν καὶ τοῖς σὺν αὐτῷ οὖσιν

passages.text: Then Jesus declared, “The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to them.\r\nHe said, “God made the Sabbath for people.\r\nGod did not make people for the Sabbath.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Τὸ σάββατον διὰ τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἐγένετο καὶ οὐχ ὁ ἄνθρωπος διὰ τὸ σάββατον

passages.text: Therefore, the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of Man.
Jesus has authority.
Jesus is Lord.
Jesus is Lord over the Sabbath.
passages.original: ὥστε κύριός ἐστιν ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου καὶ τοῦ σαββάτου
